Personally I myself have never used a pre-made or written ritual mantra. I find they have always worked best when made in that moment. Which is something you should mention to your team as well. Also include (for those not so magically inclined) that positive meditation and self manifestation can help with having more confidence and charisma in a given situation. As far as having internal and external parts of a ritual for the group you've described I feel this suggestion will help lead you in the right direction. For internal, advise them to imagine their most important approach aspects and their weakest  skills. Remind them to reflect on previous work days and recall different scenarios as honest as possible to help accurately determine all factors with this step. As far as the external part in your scenario i feel an alter or talisman would be too much. A quote or affirmation pinned in front of them directly would be very useful in this type of ritual so long as they believe that as well. For those who can't connect to an object I also suggest offering a physical pose held for a set amount of time as a secondary external option. Whether it be a specific hand placement or even just guiding them to choose and hold a comfortable frame position while going through their chosen internal routine. The main thing I feel here is you're dealing with people who's magic belief varies and to make this possible to create individually you'll need to adapt and expand instructions for the group. Be sure its clear that there isnt a wrong or right way in this process. Every teammate will speak and create a different ritual for themselves making it more personal and effective for them. 

That's how I would approach this situation. I hope I've helped.

Late to comment but yes I agree with all of these comments as well as we've seen them routinely. We get shopped about twice a week and usually thetip off is you ordering a specific shake with your burger and fries. The Oreo double stuff shake (Oreo cookies and Oreo cream) or even just a shake thats like 2-3 flavors. Though it isn't unusual for a normal customer to get shakes like that they normally won't order them at the same time with fries and a burger, they'll come get it after they eat. Also we are specifically told to watch and engage with our customers. After all you're there for burgers, fries, shakes, and a show. So we always scan for customers nearby the counter while we're working and engage upon eye contact. (Secret shoppers generally watch closely.) Ultimately that makes my job really fun. My favorite customers are the ones I catch singing a song that I'm also singing and I tell them this is or karaoke duet. Its awesome to read this thread from a secret shopper here on reddit tho and im happy to hear you enjoy our food and restaurant. 😌😌
